title: Why Mitochondria Have Their Own DNA
subject: biology

beats.narration: Inside every cell in your body sits a tiny power plant with its own DNA. Why?
beats.claim: cells contain an organelle that keeps its own DNA
beats.visual_question: why would a power plant need its own genetic code?
beats.visual_answer: the cell interior with the mitochondrion singled out as the stranger inside

beats.narration: Mitochondria burn sugar to make ATP, the energy coin of life. But they hold a strange secret.
beats.claim: mitochondria produce ATP and carry a hidden anomaly
beats.visual_question: what is strange about this organelle?
beats.visual_answer: macro mitochondrion with folded cristae, drawn closer than comfortable

beats.narration: Every mitochondrion keeps a ring of DNA, separate from the nucleus. Human mitochondrial DNA carries just 37 genes.
beats.claim: mitochondria hold their own circular DNA with 37 genes in humans
beats.visual_answer: a cutaway showing cristae, matrix, and a small circular DNA ring apart from the nucleus

beats.narration: About 1.5 billion years ago a large cell swallowed a bacterium, and kept it, instead of digesting it.
beats.claim: mitochondria began as a swallowed bacterium about 1.5 billion years ago
beats.visual_question: where did the separate DNA come from?
beats.visual_answer: endosymbiosis sequence: host cell engulfs a bacterium, and the pair becomes one

beats.narration: The guest stayed, copying itself, keeping its own membrane, its own ribosomes, and its own DNA.
beats.claim: mitochondria kept bacterial traits: double membrane, own ribosomes, own DNA
beats.visual_question: what bacterial traits did the tenant keep?
beats.visual_answer: diagram of the double membrane with its own ribosomes and DNA ring annotated

beats.narration: Mitochondrial DNA passes almost entirely through the mother. Your mitochondrial genome is your mother's line, unchanged by fathers.
beats.claim: mitochondrial DNA is inherited through the maternal line
beats.visual_answer: egg carrying mitochondria forward while the sperm contributes none

beats.narration: So the power plant in your cells was never really yours. It is a 1.5-billion-year-old tenant, still dividing.
beats.claim: the mitochondrion is a 1.5-billion-year-old tenant still dividing in your cells
beats.visual_question: what should you see when you think of your own cells now?
beats.visual_answer: the cell at rest with mitochondria quietly dividing inside it
